title: Redwood POC scoping w/ Northshore Health - security pilot
summary: POC scoping focused on security/compliance requirements for a healthcare pilot. Discussed SOC 2/ISO expectations, SSO/SAML & RBAC, audit logging and retention, KMS/HSM for key management, BAA/HIPAA considerations, and workload sizing for benchmark runs. Agreed on pilot success criteria, benchmark dataset and timeline; next steps include sharing security docs, BAA draft, and scheduling benchmark run week of 2026-04-06.
next_steps: Redwood: share SOC 2 + ISO summaries and network diagrams (Maya)
Redwood: send BAA draft and HIPAA notes (Erika)
SE: schedule benchmark run w/ sample prompts and token budget (Jonas)
Customer: provide redacted sample dataset and expected QPS profile (Samir)
Schedule follow-up to review benchmark results (tentative 2026-04-13)
action_items: Maya Patel: email SOC2 + ISO docs and network diagram by 2026-03-24
Erika Lopez: attach BAA template and high-level HIPAA guide by 2026-03-25
Jonas Wu: prepare benchmark plan (2k prompts, ~50–100 concurrent clients) and test script by 2026-03-30
Samir Khan: deliver redacted sample prompts and expected concurrency profile by 2026-03-29
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): okay everyone on the call? hey thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood - with Jonas our SE and Erika from CS. um the goal today is to scope the POC for Northshore's security pilot. we want to cover success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and obviously compliance asks - SOC 2, ISO and HIPAA related stuff.
[00:18] Claire (Head InfoSec): hi thanks, yes main ask is to validate that the pilot will not expose PHI and that auditability and key management meet our SOC 2/ISO checklist. we'll also need SSO tied to our IdP (SAML) and strict RBAC.
[00:32] Jonas (SE): got it. quick clarification on pilot scope — are you planning to use hosted Redwood API or private deployment inside a VPC? that impacts KMS options and audit log access.
[00:42] Aaron (CTO): we prefer hosted to start for speed but we need guarantees around data residency and a BAA. if hosted doesn't meet latency/cost we can consider Dedicated or Private.
[00:53] Maya: totally fair. for the pilot we usually run a 2–4 week scoping with benchmarks; success criteria typically: security signoff, latency under target X, throughput to support your peak requests, and no PII leakage in logs. what's your latency SLO?
[01:08] Samir (Platform): we're hoping for sub-500ms p95 for short prompts (<256 tokens) when routed to a GPU-backed instance. for longer context it's okay to be higher. also we expect ~50 concurrent active users during peak, translating to roughly 80 requests/sec with batching.
[01:27] Jonas: that helps. for benchmarking we can simulate 100QPS with 50 clients and a mix of prompt sizes — we'll measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and tail latency. we can run both hosted and dedicated profiles to compare.
[01:42] Claire: important: audit logs must show per-token costs tied to tokens, user identity mapping (SSO), and immutable entries for any admin actions. retention policy needs to be 1 year minimum but must be configurable; also need alerts on anomalous access.
[01:58] Jonas: Redwood supports structured audit logs and we can export to your SIEM. small caveat — some auto-telemetry fields may have hashed values; we can work with you to ensure no PHI is logged.
[02:10] Lena (Compliance): are you SOC 2 type II and do you have an ISO 27001 certification? we need evidence for both or at least roadmap for ISO and SOC 2 reports.
[02:19] Maya: Redwood has SOC 2 type II report and ISO 27001 in progress — we can send the SOC 2 attestation and a current ISO scope doc.
[02:26] Aaron: also key mgmt — do you support customer-managed keys with HSM? either via KMS or bring-your-own-key?
[02:33] Jonas: yes, Dedicated and Private deployments support CMK in major KMS providers; for hosted we offer envelope encryption and can integrate with customer KMS for dedicated contracts. HSM-backed keys are supported in Private setups.
[02:44] Claire: SSO — we use Okta, SAML-based. need SCIM and SAML provisioning and role mapping. RBAC must allow restricting access to models, logs, and billing.
[02:54] Jonas: SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning is standard; we can provision roles for read-only, deploy, admin, and billing. we'll show a demo of RBAC in the console during the follow-up.
[03:04] Samir: one operational question — can we pin model versions and have automatic fallback to a smaller quantized variant if capacity is constrained? that affects consistency for our latency tests.
[03:14] Jonas: yes, rollout policies allow pinning and fallback. during benchmarks we'll test both target model and fallback to measure degradation.
[03:22] Maya: let's talk success criteria concretely — from Redwood's side we propose: security docs reviewed and BAA signed, benchmark demonstrating p95 < 500ms for <256 token prompts on dedicated profile, ability to ingest redacted sample dataset without PHI leakage, and RBAC + SSO working end-to-end. are we aligned?
[03:40] Claire: that list looks right. add audit log export to your SIEM and one month of detailed audit logs available for immediate review.
[03:48] Lena: also we need a formal data retention config in the console and proof that logs can be purged on request.
[03:55] Jonas: we can provide a config UI and API for retention; purge requests will be handled per the BAA terms. we'll include that in the docs.
[04:04] Maya: on timelines — propose security docs and BAA by end of next week, benchmark plan by 2026-03-30, customer delivers sample prompts by 2026-03-29, run benchmarks first week of April, share results and decision meeting mid-April. does that timeline work?
[04:18] Aaron: yes that fits our procurement cadence. note that if benchmarks show unacceptable latency we'll evaluate Dedicated or Private deployment options which may need 2–4 weeks more for setup.
[04:29] Claire: any concerns around HIPAA? we need to ensure Redwood can sign the BAA and that hosted telemetry is PHI-free.
[04:36] Erika (CSM): Redwood routinely signs BAAs; we'll put the draft in the follow-up packet and highlight telemetry fields that are suppressed or hashed.
[04:45] Samir: for the benchmark workload — here's our expected token distribution: 60% short prompts (~64 tokens), 30% medium (~256 tokens), 10% long (~1k tokens). average tokens per request about 210, total throughput target 80 req/s, bursts to 150 req/s for 30s.
[05:03] Jonas: perfect. we'll simulate that profile and also run a persistence test for KV cache warmup; that will show steady-state token cost and latency improvement with caching.
[05:13] Maya: any competitor comparisons to note? Claire previously evaluated Anthropic and Bedrock, main concerns were cost and integration complexity. we can run comparative numbers in the benchmark if helpful.
[05:25] Claire: yes please include rough cost estimates and a short note on integration effort.
[05:30] Maya: ok last part — next steps recap then we can wrap.
[05:34] Jonas: recap — Redwood to send SOC2 docs, ISO status, network diagram; Erika to share BAA draft and HIPAA guide; Jonas to send benchmark plan and script; Samir to share sample prompts and concurrency profile; schedule benchmark week of 2026-04-06 and follow-up 2026-04-13.
[05:52] Aaron: thanks all. one more ask — can you include audit log examples with schema and retention config in the packet?
[05:59] Jonas: yes will include sample audit log JSON and SIEM mapping.
[06:04] Maya: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet by Tuesday.
[06:08] Claire: thanks, bye.

Note: transcription contains occasional mis-attributions and minor recognition errors (e.g., "KMS" sometimes transcribed as "KMSes").
